findings.claim: Endpoint-integrated contrasts for the global centroid are weak and mostly null: centroid_x and centroid_z have confidence intervals spanning zero with q>0.25, while centroid_y shows a small negative integrated effect (q~0.014) with only ~21% positive batches. These are selection-window endpoint contrasts, not absolute geometric descriptors or physical interaction energies.

Shape (second-moment) endpoint contrasts are the strongest and most consistent signals: shape_yy has a negative integrated effect with q~1.5e-5 and 0% positive batches, shape_xx is negative with q~8e-4 and ~7% positive batches, and shape_zz is negative but weaker (q~0.067). The direction is a signed favorable-versus-comparison contrast at observed nodes over the observed window, not an absolute reward target.

Continuous contrast functions over the complete observed support are non-monotone: landmark local features show multiple sign changes (e.g. 4-10 sign changes) and strong sign conflicts, with first-rate and last-rate z-scores of opposite sign and large magnitude, and no accepted polynomial fit (extrapolation disallowed). This supports a time-conditioned rather than constant rule, but the curves are coordinate contrasts, not absolute reward targets.

hypotheses.direction: increase magnitude of negative shape_yy/shape_xx integrated contrast
hypotheses.falsifier: If the time-conditioned rule yields an integrated shape_yy contrast no more negative than the constant rule, or reverses sign, the hypothesis is rejected.
hypotheses.observable: endpoint-integrated shape_yy and shape_xx contrast z-scores
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned regional attention recipe that up-weights the observed-node contrast for shape_yy (and secondarily shape_xx) during the late observed window will produce a larger negative integrated shape contrast than a constant-weight rule, because the observed contrast curves change sign and rate across the window.

limitations: Recorded affinities are removed and the label prior is equal, so no final-affinity benefit can be claimed; endpoint contrasts are coordinate contrasts only.

No decoded terminal labels or descendant survival/quality credit were read, so last-record credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit and the immediate-versus-descendant comparison is unavailable.
Continuous trend rows report observed-node linear fits with extrapolation disallowed; no validated polynomial was accepted, so no extrapolation beyond the observed window is supported.
Turnover accounting, increment effects and joint diagnostics were not read in this budget; within-path change versus cohort composition remains unassessed.
